title: Increment Digits
statement:
A non-negative integer is stored one decimal digit per element, most significant digit first. Return the digits of that integer plus one.

Contract
- `digits` is non-null and non-empty; every element is between 0 and 9, and there are no leading zeros except for the single digit `[0]`.
- Return a new array holding the digits of the number plus one, again most significant first and without leading zeros. It is one element longer when every input digit is 9.
- Do not mutate `digits`, and do not convert the digits to a number type: the array may be far longer than any `long`.

Examples
- `increment(new int[]{1, 2, 9})` returns `[1, 3, 0]`.
- `increment(new int[]{9, 9})` returns `[1, 0, 0]`.
- `increment(new int[]{0})` returns `[1]`.
hints: Adding one only touches the least significant digits: it starts at the last position and carries leftwards.
Walk from the right: a 9 becomes 0 and the carry continues; the first digit that is not 9 is simply increased and you can stop.
If the walk falls off the left end, every digit was 9, so the answer is a 1 followed by zeros. Intended complexity: O(n) time for n digits and O(n) space, because the result is a new array.
inputSyntax: Input: the digits, most significant first, for example: [1, 2, 9]
